title: Charlie Christian, Minton's and the Leonard Feather label
summary: Collins insists he never tried to play like Charlie Christian, recalls hearing him at Minton's and meeting him at Monroe's Uptown House, and objects to being labeled Christian-inspired.

blocks.x: And I just always heard like this, you know. So as I say, it was just a gift, I guess, you know. But coming back to Charlie Christian, I heard Dizzy say -- Dizzy's the only one who really tells the truth about -- I don't say tell the truth. Who really is aware what happened. I never tried

to play like Charlie Christian. I've been given credit for playing like Charlie or being influenced by Charlie, but I never -- I always admired his playing, he was a tremendous guitarist. But we thought differently, and I would go to hear Charlie every night in Minton's. That's when Dizzy was there, and Joe Guy and Monk. Let's see, the bass player was Nick Finton, and the saxophone player's name was Scotty.

And every night I would go there because Charlie would come by and play, and I admired his play. But I never wanted to play like him, because I heard different things, you know. His was a very exciting style and everybody just loved him, including me. And all the guitarists just jumped on his style. But I had to be me, and I guess I'm stubborn, you know. But I'm still getting a little ahead of my story because I want to tell you when I first met Charlie I had been on the road with Fletcher Henderson, and I'll get to a story about Fletcher. But I had been on the road with Fletcher Henderson and I got in town this night and I went to Monroe's Uptown House. And Charlie was playing, and I had my guitar and I started chording and playing for him, and he turned around and he stopped playing and he stopped and looked at what I was doing, because I was -- he liked what I was doing. You know, this was how I met him.
But it was a mutual admiration thing. But
MS. WILLARD: It wasn't Like (inaudible) Leonard Feather's Encyclopedia of Jazz says, when he calls you Christian - inspired.
No, no, I -- listen, always Leonard -- you know, I love him but sometimes I question some of the things he says, especially about me, and my age.
